one_liner: Cooks for a living at scale - hotels, restaurants, canteens, cloud kitchens, ships.
job_roles: Commis Chef | Chef de Partie | Cook | Baker | Pastry Chef | Butcher | Cloud Kitchen Cook | Institutional & Canteen Cook | Private & Domestic Cook | Ship's Cook
entrance_exams: NCHMCT JEE | State hotel management institute admissions
self_emp_route: Own restaurant, cloud kitchen, catering business or tiffin service. Catering and cloud kitchens need far less capital than a restaurant and are the realistic first step; this is also where almost all the money in the profession is.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. Cooking is heat, hands, timing and taste in a physical kitchen, and no part of it is a text or image problem. Recipe generation touches menu development, which is a small slice of one senior role. The real technological pressure on this profession is different and worth naming: cloud kitchens and central production units are deskilling the line, turning cooks into assemblers of components made elsewhere.
role_spread: [Pastry Chef, Baker] higher: attention_span, conscientiousness, logical / lower: extraversion || [Institutional & Canteen Cook, Private & Domestic Cook] higher: conscientiousness, agreeableness / lower: openness, confidence || [Cloud Kitchen Cook] higher: bodily, short_term_memory, attention_span / lower: extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream, or none. Craft courses take class 10 pass; the B.Sc route needs class 12. -> training: An IHM craft course or diploma, a B.Sc Hospitality and Hotel Administration, or a kitchen apprenticeship with no certificate at all - all three are normal. -> work: Commis in a hotel or restaurant kitchen. Entry pay is low and hours are long; this is the profession's known filter. -> specialisation: A section - garde manger, butchery, bakery, Indian, continental. Specialising is what moves a cook off the entry wage.
nuances: [economics] The wide mid-career range is a real spread, not uncertainty. A hotel kitchen in a metro, a cruise line contract and a small-town restaurant pay very differently for the same skill, and the overseas route - cruise ships, the Gulf, hotel chains abroad - is why pathway is 'any' and is how many Indian chefs actually raise their income. || [demand_signal] High and among the most geographically distributed in this dataset. Every town has kitchens. That makes it one of very few skilled livelihoods genuinely available to a student who does not move to a city. || [entry_competition] Null, and it was wrong on the first pass. NCHMCT JEE was named as primary because it is the only quantified door in this sector - but this record's own entrance_exams note says most working Indian chefs never sat it, and both statements could not be true. Cooking is entered through a kitchen. The gate stays on Hotel & Restaurant Manager, where the IHM degree really is the main route.

one_liner: Serves guests food and drink and runs the room - restaurants, bars, banquets, trains, air.
job_roles: Steward | Waiter | Restaurant Captain | Bartender | Barista | Sommelier | Banquet Service Staff | Room Service Attendant | Cafe & QSR Service Crew
entrance_exams: NCHMCT JEE | State hotel management institute admissions
self_emp_route: A cafe, bar or small restaurant of your own, or a catering and bartending service for events. Bartending in particular is a genuine freelance market at weddings and parties.
ai_reason: Low AI exposure and high exposure to something else. Ordering has already moved to apps and QR menus, and Cafe & QSR Service Crew and Room Service Attendant are the roles that shrinks - but that is self-service automation, not AI. What holds is hospitality itself: reading a table, fixing a complaint, and making a guest feel looked after. Sommelier and Bartender are protected further by knowledge and personality being the product.
role_spread: [Bartender, Sommelier] higher: long_term_memory, extraversion, openness / lower: conscientiousness || [Banquet Service Staff, Cafe & QSR Service Crew] higher: bodily, conscientiousness / lower: verbal, openness || [Restaurant Captain] higher: extraversion, emotional_intelligence, confidence, emotional_stability / lower: -
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None for most service roles; class 12 for hotel management programmes. -> training: An IHM or private hospitality course, a THSC-aligned certification, or straight on-the-job training. Most enter with the last. -> work: Restaurant, hotel, cafe chain, catering company, railway or airline catering, or a cruise line. -> specialisation: Bar, wine, or supervision. Beverage specialisation is the clearest way to raise earnings inside service.
review_reason: No sourced wage figure for Indian hospitality service staff, and the record cannot show tips, service charge or the overseas premium - which between them are much of the real income. Cruise line and Gulf contract pay in particular is the difference between this being a low-wage job and a genuine earner, and no figure for it was found.
nuances: [economics] Fails nothing on the filter but sits low, and the record should be read with tips and service charge in mind - neither is captured here and both are material in hotels and premium restaurants. The overseas route, especially cruise lines and the Gulf, is again where earnings change. || [demand_signal] High and permanently entry-friendly. This profession, along with retail in Sector 5, is one of the main places an Indian school-leaver with no qualification actually finds formal-sector work.

one_liner: Keeps rooms, buildings and linen clean and ready - hotels, hospitals, offices, homestays.
job_roles: Housekeeping Attendant | Room Attendant | Housekeeping Supervisor | Laundry Supervisor | Linen & Uniform Room Attendant | Public Area Attendant | Facility Housekeeping Executive | Hospital Housekeeping Attendant | Homestay & Guesthouse Caretaker | Hospital Cleaner | Office Cleaner | Building Caretaker
self_emp_route: A small housekeeping or facility services contract - a team, supplies and a client. It is a low-capital services business and it is how supervisors in this trade raise their income.
ai_reason: Effectively unexposed to AI, and this is another case where naming AI is the wrong risk. Cleaning a room is physical work in an unstructured space. The technology that matters is mechanised cleaning equipment, which raises output per worker rather than replacing the worker, and scheduling software, which has already changed how contract housekeeping is managed.
role_spread: [Hospital Housekeeping Attendant] higher: conscientiousness, attention_span / lower: extraversion, openness || [Housekeeping Supervisor, Facility Housekeeping Executive] higher: verbal, conscientiousness, logical / lower: bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Class 8 or 10 is typical. -> training: On-the-job, or a short THSC-aligned housekeeping certification. Hospital housekeeping requires infection-control training. -> work: Hotel, hospital, facility management contractor, corporate office or serviced apartment. Most of it is contract employment through an agency rather than direct. -> progression: Supervisor, then executive. Or run a homestay or a small housekeeping contract of your own.
review_reason: No sourced wage figure for Indian housekeeping staff, and the more important missing distinction is between direct hotel employment and agency contract employment, which is where pay, provident fund and security actually differ. No figure either for what a small housekeeping contract earns, which is the named route up.
nuances: [economics] Fails the compensation filter, and it is one of the largest formal-sector entry occupations available to Indian women without qualifications. Almost all of it is CONTRACT employment through a facility management agency rather than direct employment by the hotel or hospital, which determines pay, benefits and job security more than the employer's name does. || [demand_signal] High and growing with organised retail, hospitals, offices and hotels. It is also one of the few occupations in this dataset where formalisation is genuinely increasing - facility management contracting has moved a large amount of this work from informal to at least nominally formal employment.

one_liner: Runs the place - rooms, covers, staff, cost, and what happens when a guest is unhappy.
job_roles: Front Office Executive | Guest Relations Executive | Duty Manager | Restaurant Manager | Food & Beverage Manager | Revenue & Reservations Executive | Banquet & Events Manager | Resort Operations Executive | Hostel & Homestay Manager
entrance_exams: NCHMCT JEE | State hotel management institute admissions
self_emp_route: Own restaurant, homestay, boutique hotel or cloud kitchen brand. Very common in this profession, and the operational knowledge transfers directly - which is why hospitality graduates start businesses at a higher rate than most.
ai_reason: Moderately exposed on the desk and protected on the floor. Revenue & Reservations Executive is the most exposed role - dynamic pricing is already algorithmic and improving - and routine reservations and enquiry handling have largely moved to booking platforms and chat. Duty Manager, Front Office Executive and Restaurant Manager are protected by being the person physically accountable when something goes wrong at eleven at night.
role_spread: [Revenue & Reservations Executive] higher: logical, reasoning, attention_span / lower: bodily || [Front Office Executive, Guest Relations Executive] higher: extraversion, emotional_intelligence, confidence / lower: logical
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> entrance_exam: NCHMCT JEE for the Institutes of Hotel Management, or a state or private institute admission. -> degree: B.Sc Hospitality and Hotel Administration (3 years), or any degree plus hotel experience. -> work: Management trainee or front office executive, then a section. Progression is by rotating through departments.
nuances: [entry_competition] Null. NCHMCT JEE was recorded here on the first pass and removed on review: this record is mid_stream_entry 'after_any_degree', its own path_to_entry says 'any degree plus hotel experience', and the exam offers over 12,000 seats. A gate that admits any graduate and is not scarce is not the thing that determines who reaches the profession. || [economics] The employed range is Indian. The profession's real economics for many people are overseas - Gulf hotels, cruise lines and international chains - and that pathway is a large part of why students choose hotel management. It is why pathway is 'any' and it is not visible in these numbers. || [demand_signal] High, and unusually resilient in a specific way: hospitality collapsed completely during the pandemic and rebuilt, and the sector's hiring now runs ahead of the supply of trained people because a cohort left the industry and did not return.

one_liner: Plans, sells and guides travel - itineraries, tickets, tours and the people on them.
job_roles: Travel Consultant | Tour Operator | Tour Guide | Destination Specialist | Ticketing & Reservations Executive | Travel Sales Executive | Tour Manager | Pilgrimage & Cultural Tour Coordinator | Corporate Travel Coordinator
entrance_exams: Ministry of Tourism regional guide training and licensing | IATA and travel agency certifications
self_emp_route: An independent tour operation, a niche travel business - wildlife, pilgrimage, adventure, weddings abroad - or freelance guiding. Low capital and high dependence on repeat customers and reviews.
ai_reason: The most AI-exposed profession in this sector, and the damage arrived before AI did. Ticketing & Reservations Executive and Travel Consultant lost their market to online booking over two decades, and language models finish the job on itinerary planning and destination advice - both are high-retrievable-knowledge tasks. What survives is physical presence and accountability: Tour Guide, licensed and standing in front of the monument, and Tour Manager, responsible for thirty people in a foreign country when something goes wrong.
role_spread: [Tour Guide, Pilgrimage & Cultural Tour Coordinator] higher: verbal, long_term_memory, extraversion / lower: logical || [Ticketing & Reservations Executive, Corporate Travel Coordinator] higher: conscientiousness, attention_span, logical / lower: openness || [Tour Manager] higher: extraversion, conscientiousness / lower: openness, emotional_stability
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. A second language is worth more than a stream in this profession. -> training: BA or diploma in Travel and Tourism, an IATA-recognised course for ticketing, or a Ministry of Tourism guide training programme. -> licence: For guiding at protected monuments, a Ministry of Tourism or state tourism department guide licence. -> work: Travel agency, tour operator, online travel platform, a hotel's travel desk, or independent guiding.
nuances: [demand_signal] Moderate, and the composition has changed completely rather than the level. Indian domestic and outbound travel volumes are at record highs while the number of people employed selling travel has fallen - the value moved to platforms. Growth is in experiences and guiding, not in agency work. || [licensing_body] Null at profession level, but guiding at protected monuments does require a Ministry of Tourism or state licence. It is a permission to work at specific sites rather than a professional register, which is why the field stays null.

one_liner: Makes an event happen - weddings, conferences, concerts, exhibitions, sport.
job_roles: Event Coordinator | Wedding Planner | Conference & MICE Executive | Exhibition & Trade Fair Coordinator | Venue Operations Executive | Sponsorship & Partnerships Executive | Production Coordinator (Events) | Sports Event Coordinator | Catering Sales Executive
self_emp_route: Own event or wedding planning business. Extremely common in this profession, needs little capital, and runs on a vendor network and referrals rather than on marketing.
ai_reason: Low to moderate exposure. Planning documents, run sheets, budgets and vendor briefs generate well, and Conference & MICE Executive work is the most exposed. But an event is a physical thing that happens once at a fixed time, and Production Coordinator (Events) and Venue Operations Executive are protected absolutely by that. Wedding Planner is protected by managing two families through the most emotionally loaded purchase of their lives, which no model is going to be trusted with.
role_spread: [Wedding Planner] higher: emotional_intelligence, extraversion / lower: logical, emotional_stability || [Sponsorship & Partnerships Executive, Catering Sales Executive] higher: verbal, confidence, extraversion / lower: attention_span || [Production Coordinator (Events), Venue Operations Executive] higher: conscientiousness, spatial, bodily / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: Any bachelor's degree; event management, hospitality and mass communication are common. None is required. -> work: Event company, a hotel's banquet team, a wedding planning firm, an exhibition organiser, or a brand's activation team. Entry is usually as a coordinator on live events. -> independence: Own event or wedding planning business - the standard destination, and one that needs relationships with vendors more than capital.
nuances: [professional_sector] Promised here from Sector 5, and the placement is arguable in the other direction. An event company is a business and event management is project management - but the object of concern is a HOSTED EXPERIENCE for guests, which is what this sector is about, and event management in India sits inside hospitality commercially, in hotels and banquet venues. || [demand_signal] High, and it rests substantially on the Indian wedding market rather than on corporate events. That makes the work seasonal, family-facing and spread across smaller cities rather than concentrated in metros.

one_liner: Keeps an aircraft cabin safe and its passengers looked after - a safety job that serves food.
job_roles: Cabin Crew | Flight Attendant | In-flight Service Attendant | Cabin Crew Trainer | In-flight Supervisor | Ground Service & Guest Handling Executive | Charter & Private Jet Cabin Attendant
entrance_exams: Airline cabin crew recruitment (DGCA-approved training) | Private aviation academy courses
ai_reason: Low exposure, and the reason is the one most people get wrong about this job. It looks like service work; it is legally a SAFETY role. Cabin crew are on board because regulation requires trained humans to evacuate an aircraft in ninety seconds, and no amount of automation changes that requirement. The service element could be reduced; the safety minimum cannot.
role_spread: [Cabin Crew Trainer] higher: verbal, conscientiousness, confidence, emotional_stability / lower: - || [Ground Service & Guest Handling Executive] higher: extraversion, conscientiousness, bodily, emotional_stability / lower: -
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Class 12 in any stream. English fluency is required and a second language helps. -> physical_eligibility: Airline height, reach, weight and medical criteria, including vision and swimming. These are absolute and screen out a large number of applicants before anything else is assessed. -> selection: Airline assessment day - group activity, personal interview, grooming and communication. Not an examination and not published. -> training: Airline ab-initio training against a DGCA-approved syllabus, ending in a Cabin Crew Member certification. Safety and emergency procedure is the bulk of it.
